{{short description|Mexican physicist}}
[[File:Julia Tagüeña-Parga.jpg|thumb|]]
'''Julia Tagüeña Parga''' (born 21 October 1948) is a Mexican physicist from the School of Science at the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] (UNAM) and [[Doctor of Science]] from the [[University of Oxford]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Julia Tagüeña Parga "Promotora de la ciencia por convicción"|url=http://sntimp.net/publica/hombresMujere.aspx?llave=37|access-date=2020-07-01|website=sntimp.net|archive-date=2020-07-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200703175310/http://sntimp.net/publica/hombresMujere.aspx?llave=37|url-status=dead}}</ref>

She was one of the Directors for Scientific Development at the [[Consejo Nacional de Ciencia y Tecnología (Mexico)|Mexican National Council of Science and Technology]] (CONACYT) from 2013 to 2018,  and was General Director of Mexico's Science and Technology Consulting Forum (2018-2020).<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=ISRES'2020 - Home|url=https://www.ier.unam.mx/~eogm/isres2020/cv-jtp.html|access-date=2020-07-01|website=www.ier.unam.mx}}</ref> The main goals of the Forum is to act as an independent advisor of how science and technology should be integrated into Mexican laws (both at the state and federal level.) The Forum also acts an independent advisor to Mexico's Executive power and to Conacyt.

== Life and career ==
Tagüeña was born in [[Frýdlant|Frydland]], [[Czechoslovakia]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|title=Julia Tagüeña Parga|url=https://lideresmexicanos.com/300/julia-taguena-parga/|access-date=2020-07-01|website=Líderes Mexicanos|archive-date=2021-09-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210904135259/https://lideresmexicanos.com/300/julia-taguena-parga/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Her father, Manuel Tagüeña, was a physicist, and her mother, Carmen Parga, studied philosophy.<ref name=":0" /> Tagüeña is married.<ref name=":4" />

Tagüeña studied Physics at the National Autonomous University of Mexico.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Dra. Julia Tagüeña {{!}} Foro Consultivo|url=https://www.foroconsultivo.org.mx/FCCyT/coordinadores-generales/dra-julia-tag%C3%BCe%C3%B1a|access-date=2020-07-01|website=www.foroconsultivo.org.mx}}</ref> She obtained a PhD at Oxford University.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Julia Tagüeña|url=https://conicyt.cl/gendersummit12/en/personas/julia-taguena-parga/|access-date=2020-07-01|website=Gender Summit 12|language=en-US}}</ref> Her main field of research are [[solid-state physics]] and [[Renewable energy|renewable energies]].<ref name=":1" /> Tagüeña has written 11 textbooks for high school and undergraduate students and published over 50 articles on solid state research in international journals.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Tagüeña Parga, Julia {{!}} Academia de Ciencias de Morelos|url=http://www.acmor.org.mx/?q=users/tag%C3%BCe%C3%B1a-parga-julia|access-date=2020-07-01|website=www.acmor.org.mx|language=es}}</ref>

For over 25 years Tagüeña has been a research professor at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tagüeña Parga, Julia|url=http://www.acmor.org.mx/?q=users/tagüeña-parga-julia|access-date=2020-07-01|website=Academia de Ciencias de Morelos}}</ref>

From 2002 to 2005, Tagüeña held the position of the Executive Directorate of the Network for the Popularization of Science and Technology for Latin America and the Caribbean (RedPOP).<ref name=":3"/> Between 2004 and 2008, Tagüeña was Director General for the Dissemination of Science in the UNAM.<ref name=":2" />

From 2005 to 2007, she was vice president of the Mexican Association of Museums and Science and Technology Centers.<ref name=":3" /> In 2009-2010, Tagüeña was a Secretary of Morelos Academy of Sciences.<ref name=":2" />

From 2010 to 2012, she served as a president of the Mexican Society for the Dissemination of Science and Technology.<ref name=":3" />

For the short period from November 2012 to January 2013 Tagüeña was a Director of the UNAM Energy Research Center, and until March 2013 she was in charge of the office of the Institute of Renewable Energies.<ref name=":3" />

From 2013 to 2018 Tagüeña was the Deputy General Director for Scientific Development at the [[Consejo Nacional de Ciencia y Tecnología (Mexico)|Mexican National Council of Science and Technology]].<ref name=":1"/> In January 2019, Tagüeña was appointed as a general coordinator of the Scientific and Technological Advisory Forum and will held this position until 31 December 2020.<ref name=":3" />
